newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks drift down in morning after higher start.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks drift down in morning after higher start.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks drifted lower on Wednesday morning, shedding early gains as sentiment remained cautious following the market's recent shakeout and continued concerns about Chinese paramount leader Deng Xiaoping's health.
The Hang Seng Index was down 46.99 points, or 0.36 percent, at 13,055.95, after rising to an early high of 13,145.43.
Turnover was HK$1.76 billion after the first 45 minutes of trade.
"Things looked a little better early on but there is still a slight amount of continued worry about Deng," said Kent Rossiter, institutional sales manager at Nikko Securities.
"We are seeing a shift out of Hong Kong. People are hesitant to get in now," he added.
As of Tuesday's close, the index was down 558 points compared with its February 5 close ahead of Chinese New Year.
Boby Ho, dealing manager at GK Goh Securities, said he expected the market to continue drifting lower in the near term.
"I think in the medium term we will have quite a long consolidation period," he added. "Deng's health is still a major concern in the market so everybody seems pretty cautious.

The health of China's 92-year-old patriarch has stirred intense speculation among Japanese and Hong Kong newspapers. Traders said 13,000 points still seemed to provide good support for the Hang Seng Index.
"Until we get fresh news domestically we are going to trade sideways," said one.
Shares in HSBC Holdings recovered from Tuesday's decline, rising HK$1.00 to HK$184.50. Also in the banking sector, Bank of East Asia added HK$0.20 to HK$33.50.
Property stocks remained under pressure. Henderson Land fell HK$1.25 to HK$67.75 and New World Development slumped HK$0.90 to HK$46.20.
Hongkong and Shanghai Hotels was steady at HK$13.90. The company is due to report its final results later on Wednesday.
The consensus market forecast is 27 percent earnings growth. In 1995, the company reported attributable profit of HK$652 million.
